sources.title: Democratic Republic of Congo Level 3 Emergency - Upsurge in Conflict, Humanitarian Situation Report No. 5, 1-15 May 2025
sources.organization: UNICEF Democratic Republic of the Congo
sources.temporal_coverage: Humanitarian events and response reported for 1-15 May 2025, with selected response totals since the crisis began.
sources.methodology: UNICEF situation monitoring and partner-reported humanitarian response results.
sources.limitations: Operational reporting; some response figures are cumulative and are not independent evaluations.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS Country Brief: Democratic Republic of the Congo (reference date 24 June 2026)
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, Global Information and Early Warning System
sources.temporal_coverage: Seasonal crop assessments and food-security data through June 2026; rainfall outlook for June-October 2026.
sources.methodology: FAO GIEWS synthesis of crop, forecast, IPC and supply data.
sources.limitations: Country brief; forecast resolution and intervention impact evaluation are not provided.

claims.locator: PDF p. 1, highlights; PDF p. 2, situation overview
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reports flooding in Kasaba village, Fizi Territory, South Kivu, reportedly killed 62 people, including 47 children; it sent Red Cross Tanganyika to assess and identify response.
claims.limitations: Local officials are cited; the report does not attribute the flood to climate change.

claims.locator: PDF p. 2, situation overview and humanitarian needs
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reports that fighting in Kalehe, Walungu, Fizi and Mwenga displaced civilians in South Kivu; ADF attacks in Fungula and Bapere, Lubero Territory, killed more than 20 people.
claims.limitations: Conflict reporting does not establish climate as a driver of these attacks or displacement.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNICEF attributes forced flight and fatalities to armed clashes and attacks.

claims.locator: PDF p. 1, highlights; PDF p. 2, cholera and response update
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF says IDP returns extended cholera into areas with poor WASH infrastructure, complicating response; its UNiRR reached 5,352 households with WASH and shelter kits and provided free primary care in four health zones.
claims.limitations: Agency-reported outputs are not independent measures of effectiveness or durable resilience.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNICEF states that IDP returns extended the outbreak into poorer-WASH areas and complicated response.

claims.locator: Reference date 24 June 2026, cereal production and climate outlook
claims.paraphrase: FAO's June 2026 brief notes anticipated El Niño conditions and forecasts for below-average June-October rainfall, while describing main-season maize planting in northern and central regions.
claims.scenario: Anticipated El Niño; seasonal rainfall forecast below average for June-October 2026.
claims.limitations: The brief does not state the forecast's subnational resolution or report realized crop loss from this outlook.

claims.locator: Reference date 24 June 2026, cereal production and climate outlook
claims.paraphrase: FAO says eastern conflict and displacement restricted field access and disrupted agriculture; the 2026 main-season maize area was estimated below its five-year average, while forecast rainfall may separately affect crop development.
claims.limitations: FAO attributes the area-planted shortfall to conflict access constraints, not forecast rainfall; interaction is not estimated.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: FAO names climate shocks, conflict and displacement as concurrent production pressures, while attributing field-access disruption to conflict.

claims.paraphrase: FAO reports supporting 55,500 crisis-affected families in North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri and Tanganyika with a USD 10 million allocation, seeds, tools, livelihood inputs and cash assistance.
claims.limitations: FAO reports ongoing assistance, not an independent evaluation of reach or resilience outcomes.

access_audit.notes: Opened the official 10-page PDF and reviewed pp. 1-3 for the Kasaba flood report, conflict/displacement, WASH/outbreak and UNiRR results.

access_audit.locator: FAO GIEWS page, reference date 24 June 2026, cereal production and climate outlook sections
access_audit.notes: Read the full official FAO GIEWS country brief including forecast, crop-area assessment, conflict/access discussion and food-security response.

search_audit.query: DRC 2025 local flood vulnerability named site South Kivu Fizi Kasaba UNICEF report
search_audit.outcome: UNICEF reports a fatal flood in Kasaba village, Fizi Territory, and ongoing conflict-related service and displacement pressures in eastern provinces; flood account is not climate-attributed.

search_audit.query: DRC climate shocks conflict displacement field access agriculture FAO 2026 crop forecast
search_audit.outcome: FAO identifies climate shocks alongside conflict/displacement as cereal-production pressures and specifically states conflict-related displacement and restricted field access disrupted agriculture; it does not estimate climate-conflict interaction.

search_audit.query: eastern DRC armed conflict humanitarian access health WASH services 2025 UNICEF report
search_audit.outcome: UNICEF documents fighting-driven civilian flight, IDP returns extending cholera into low-WASH areas and complicating response, and emergency service delivery constraints.

search_audit.query: DRC 2026 resilience response capacity community local livelihoods seeds cash water response FAO UNICEF
search_audit.outcome: UNICEF reports targeted WASH and emergency-health outputs; FAO reports seed, tool, livelihood-input and cash support for 55,500 families in four eastern provinces. Neither source evaluates durable resilience impact.

gaps: UNICEF reports the Kasaba flood from local officials but does not attribute it to climate change or provide a detailed loss assessment.

FAO's June 2026 rainfall forecast is not spatially resolved in the brief; the source attributes reduced planting area to conflict-related access constraints and does not estimate interactions with climate forecasts.
UNICEF and FAO operational counts are publisher-reported outputs, not independent evaluations of durable adaptation, coverage equity or peace outcomes.
This new evidence remains concentrated in South Kivu and selected eastern provinces; it does not close the baseline's large subnational climate-FCV evidence gaps elsewhere in DRC.
